question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (4)
solution:
The correct answer is '**thinking**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The passage describes how Sudama always kept Krishna in his heart and soul. 
 
• The appropriate verb should reflect maintaining Krishna in his thoughts. 
 
• "**Thinking**" fits well as it indicates Sudama frequently kept Krishna in his mind. 
 
• Other options ("**waiting**", "**inspecting**", "**sinking**") do not fit the context of maintaining closeness through thoughts. 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: * The two, Sudama and Krishna, were (1) **inseparable**__. To date, their oneness is an example of true friendship ahead of the planet. This is often the rationale why they are remembered (2) __**on**__ the auspicious day of Friendship. Even after losing touch for several years after finishing their studies together, they did not (3) __**leave**__ the hope of meeting again. Sudama always had lord Krishna in his heart and soul and kept (4) __**thinking**__ of him until they met again. The entire incident when Sudama met Krishna after numerous years is so (5) _______ and unforgettable. * 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** __Additional Information__ ** 

 
• Waiting (इंतजार): "Waiting" implies expecting someone to come or something to happen, which does not align with the context of keeping someone in one's heart. 
 
• Inspecting (निरीक्षण): "Inspecting" means looking at something closely, which does not fit here. 
 
• Sinking (डूबना): "Sinking" means going down below the surface of something, especially water, which is not relevant here.
